gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the BLUETTI Apex 300's built-in solar inputs are two XT60 ports capped at 12–60 V and 20 A each, so BLUETTI's own SORA 500 panel (Voc 49.1 V, Isc 13.31 A, MC4) can only go one panel per port: two in series reach 98.2 V and two in parallel reach 26.6 A. The base unit therefore tops out at 2 × SORA 500 (1,000 W), each needing a $29 MC4-to-XT60 cable that isn't in the Apex 300 box.
standout_why: I compared this against the cited solarwaypoint.com F3800 Plus vs DELTA Pro Ultra page and the cited energysage.com overview. Solarwaypoint doesn't cover the Apex 300. It gives the F3800 Plus as 2 × 11–165 V / 17 A and says it has no series/parallel advice. EnergySage gives the Apex 300 only as '2,400 W (more with SolarX 4K)' and 'AC-only'. It names no voltage window, no connector and no panel-count limit, and it says generally that you can pick your own panels 'as long as they fall within the power station's solar input specs'. ChatGPT's card repeats '2,400 W solar input' with no window. Nobody says the 60 V cap means one SORA 500 per port, or that the XT60 ports need an MC4 adapter. That decides how many panels and which cables go in the cart. One caveat: the third cited rival, thiswatt.com, failed to open (SSL certificate error), so I couldn't check it.
kit_items: power station: BLUETTI Apex 300 (2,764.8 Wh LFP, 3,840 W, 120/240 V). Its two XT60 solar ports take 12–60 V and 20 A, 1,200 W each.

solar panels: 2 × BLUETTI SORA 500 (500 W, Voc 49.1 V, Isc 13.31 A per Impulse Gamer). Put one panel on each XT60 port. Two in series would be 98.2 V, over the 60 V cap, and two in parallel would be 26.6 A, over the 20 A port limit.
cables: 2 × BLUETTI Solar Charging Cable (20 A MC4 to XT60), one per panel. The panel uses MC4, the Apex 300 inputs are XT60, and the Apex 300 box list has no solar cable.

not in kit, for later growth: going past 1,000 W of SORA 500 panels needs BLUETTI's SolarX 4K controller in place of the base XT60 ports. BLUETTI's own guide says to 'plan parallel panel strings rather than high-voltage series arrays' on the base unit.

findings.note: Maker's own US blog. It also says: 'Apex 300 solar input is capped at 60 V Voc—plan parallel panel strings rather than high-voltage series arrays.'

findings.note: Hintze reports no measured peak solar input because the weather was poor, and notes the unit 'lacks USB or DC ports'. The SolarX 4K figure is inconsistent within the article (4,000 W in the text, 4,200 W in the table).

findings.label: Electrical specs
findings.value: Voc 49.1 V; Vmp 40.92 V; Isc 13.31 A; Imp 12.22 A; MC4; 12.9 kg (28.4 lb); operating −25 °C to 65 °C
findings.source_title: The Bluetti Sora 500 Solar Panel Review (Andrew Paul, Impulse Gamer, 2026-08-02)
findings.note: This is a named reviewer's spec table. The BLUETTI US product page's Tech Specs section was empty, and BLUETTI's EU, UK and AU pages failed to load (redirect loop or HTTP 429).

findings.label: Panels per base-unit solar port
findings.value: 1 SORA 500 per XT60 port, 2 panels (1,000 W rated) maximum on the base unit
findings.source_title: BLUETTI Apex 300 Full Setup Guide + Impulse Gamer SORA 500 review
findings.note: Arithmetic: 2 in series = 2 × 49.1 = 98.2 V Voc, over the 60 V cap. 2 in parallel = 2 × 13.31 = 26.62 A Isc (Imp 24.44 A), over the 20 A per-port limit. One panel is 49.1 V and 13.31 A, inside 12–60 V and 20 A, with 10.9 V of Voc headroom at STC.

findings.note: Price $849.00 that day (storecheck). The page lists no Voc, Isc or wiring guidance.
